title: The Flannan Isles Keepers (1900)
summary: Three lighthouse keepers vanish from a remote Hebridean rock in 1900 — the lamp room locked, a meal left half-eaten, and a logbook describing a storm that weather records say never happened. Every theory since has failed somewhere.

title: The Great Mull Air Mystery (1975)
summary: Pilot Peter Gibbs takes off on a Christmas Eve flight over Mull and is never found — until his body turns up months later on a hillside, unmarked by any crash. The search, the silence, and the theories that still don't add up.

title: The Arthur's Seat Coffins (1836)
summary: Seventeen miniature coffins, each holding a carefully dressed doll, found hidden in an Edinburgh cave in 1836. Eight survive in a museum today — and no one has ever agreed on who made them, or why.

title: Netta Fornario, Iona (1929)
summary: An occultist is found dead on a fairy mound on Iona in 1929 — naked but for a cloak, a cross cut into the turf beside her. What happened in her final days has never been fully explained.

title: The Overtoun Bridge Dogs
summary: For decades, dogs have leapt to their deaths from the same parapet of a bridge near Dumbarton. Folklore calls it a thin place; science offers a scent trail. Neither quite closes the case.

title: The Appin Murder (1752)
summary: A shot in a Highland wood, a hanged man who almost certainly didn't pull the trigger, and a real killer's name kept as a clan secret to this day.

title: The Gorbals Vampire (1954)
summary: Hundreds of Glasgow children stormed a Victorian necropolis one evening in 1954, armed with stakes, hunting a seven-foot vampire with iron teeth. The panic made international news — and its real origin is stranger than the monster.

title: The Lost Gold of Loch Arkaig
summary: Seven casks of Spanish gold landed on a Highland shore for the Jacobites in 1745. Most of it was never seen again — and several of the men who moved it died oddly.

title: Christie Cleek (14th century)
summary: Long before Sawney Bean, a Grampian blacksmith turned to cannibalism during a medieval famine — and was never caught. The case that likely inspired Scotland's most famous horror legend.

title: Sawney Bean: The Cannibal Who Never Was?
summary: Scotland's most famous horror story — a cannibal clan hiding in a coastal cave — has no contemporary record at all. Why did a story with no evidence become the country's best-known legend?
